summary: Verified STRICT sandwich rule (leave_groups >= 2) revert. All 8 backend tests PASSED. Chirag Patel (117) with single Mon leave on 2026-07-13: sandwich_days=0, cl_count=0, sandwich_amount=0.0, and not present in attendance sandwich_dates. Milan Tandel (1) with Mon-Fri leaves (13-17 July): sandwich_days=0, cl_count=0.5, sandwich_amount=0.0, and not in sandwich_dates. Frontend Attendance July 2026 verified visually: Milan row shows WO on days 11,12,18,19; Chirag row shows WO on days 11,12 (NO 'SW' badges for either employee). check-sandwich regressions: Fri+Mon (2026-08-07,10) correctly triggers has_sandwich=true with dates [08,09]; single Mon (08-10) returns false; Mon-Fri block returns false; Mon+Wed (no holiday between) returns false as expected.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is very large (>6900 lines). Consider splitting sandwich logic into a separate module and adding unit tests for edge cases (holidays flanked, half-day leaves, mixed leave types).
The sandwich_dates response for attendance uses employee_id as string key ('117'); ensure consistency with salary_data where employee_id can be int.
seed_data_creation: None - used existing production data for Milan (1) and Chirag (117).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Strict sandwich rule (leave_groups >= 2) is confirmed working via 8 pytest tests and visual DOM verification of Attendance grid. For future testing: salary endpoint returns {year,month,num_days,salary_data:[...]} (not a flat list). Attendance sandwich_dates keys are string employee_ids. The doubled-text array from row extraction is due to buttons containing both testid and text nodes—use every-other value or filter accordingly.
rca of the issue: Previous iteration_9 aggressive rule (leave_groups >= 1) caused single-side leaves to incorrectly sandwich adjacent weekends. Reverting to leave_groups >= 2 requires flanking leaves on BOTH sides of a weekend/holiday cluster to count as sandwich. Verified across all 6 code locations (5118, 5497, 5924, 6581, 6792, 6965).
